content:
li: Noticed oscillations when we apply hard region penalties during weekend traffic spike. p95 jumps then falls, repeat. Thinking hysteresis rather than step changes.

rachel: Yup. Hard penalties are causing preemptive fallbacks that increase cold starts, then penalty drops, traffic returns, repeat. We need smoothing.

tom: Proposal: introduce two fields in policy DSL: penalty_smoothing.window (s) and penalty_smoothing.decay (alpha). Use EWMA on recent fallback_rate to modulate penalty.

priya: Example DSL snippet: ```policy: region_penalty params: multiplier: 1.2 smoothing: { window: 300, decay: 0.15, min: 0.1, max: 2.0 } cooldown: 180``` Would that capture it?

li: Looks good. Also think we need a separate "momentum" for tenant-level penalties vs global region. Tenants with bursty workloads shouldn't flip the whole region.

rachel: Agreed. Add scope: global|region|tenant and ensure smoothing runs per-scope.

tom: Implementation detail: runtime should maintain per-scope EWMA and a separate "pending_adjustment" queue. Adjustments apply only if sustained beyond a threshold (e.g., 3 samples). Prevent thrash.

priya: What about cost vs latency tradeoffs? Smoothing reduces rapid cost wins but prevents latency regressions. We need an objective function: utility = -w_latency * delta_p95 - w_cost * delta_cost. If utility negative -> don't increase penalty.

li: Good call. Keep weights configurable by product. Default w_latency=0.7, w_cost=0.3. Product can tune per-tenant in policy metadata.

infra-bot: note: added feature-flag:runtime.penalty_smoothing.v1 (off in prod). Use sim to validate before flip.

rachel: Also: provide a "safety ramp" that caps instantaneous penalty deltas to a percent (e.g., 10% per 5m) so even with smoothing you never jump >10% in one step.

tom: For testing, sim-bot can run replay with past 7 days of telemetry and evaluate hypothetical smoothing configs. sim-bot: run 7d-replay --policy region_penalty --configs smoothing:window=300,decay=0.1,cap=0.1

sim-bot: queued replay job 8832. Expect ~15m runtime. Results will include p95_delta and embedding_token_cost_delta by tenant.

priya: UX: in Console show a "policy trend" sparkline + active smoothed value and raw signal. Also allow manual "nudge" for oncall: small override that respects smoothing (i.e., marks as high-confidence but still decays).

li: Operational guardrails: require canary rollout with delta percent (1-3%) for 1h, capture p95, fallback_rate, cold_starts. Auto-rollback if p95 > baseline + 10%.

rachel: Let's add a new telemetry metric: penalty_adjustment_rate (how often runtime changes penalty) and alert if > X per 10m. That flags thrash.

infra-bot: alert rule created: penalty_adjustment_rate > 5 per 10m -> page eng-oncall

tom: Backwards compatibility: if smoothing fields missing, runtime defaults to legacy immediate-change semantics. Migration tool should add default smoothing to archived policies.

priya: One more thought: sometimes we want immediate emergency ramp-downs (e.g., incident). Add an explicit "emergency_override" path that bypasses smoothing but requires higher auth and auditing. TTL enforced.

li: Security note: emergency_override requires 2-person approval and SSO header. Audit entry mandatory.

rachel: Action items: 1) tom to prototype EWMA adaptor in runtime (1 week) 2) priya to update DSL docs + console mocks (3 days) 3) li to add sim job and run candidate configs (after prototype) 4) infra to gate via feature flag and add alerts.

tom: I'll push a tiny RFC with implementation plan and perf constraints (constant mem per scope, eviction policy for stale scopes).

li: Thanks. If sim results look good we can roll to canary next week. Keep thread posted. :rocket:
